messages.content: Enter token-radar-01 on make.fun: build the best token launch radar from the kit in ~/workspace/makefun/token-radar-01/. Read the kit's RULES.txt and the snapshot field guide first, write our own model and dashboard (the starter is a starting point, not a winner), keep the gate's shape, and hand in a complete repo: main.ts at the root, dashboard/, screenshots/, LICENSE, owner.json. Quality over speed - it is top 10 or nothing.

Kit read. The contract: main.ts (Node 22, standard library only) reads /input/snapshot.json, writes /output/board.json (100 to 4,000 rows, ranks 1..N, implied value non-increasing by rank, every watchlist slug covered, 3 to 12 farm steps of 20 to 600 characters a row), copies dashboard/ and screenshots/ to /output, and writes dossier.json with the kit's vendored buildDossier. The gate checks seven rows; the judge weighs, in order: a working radar with watchlist coverage, a value model derived from the snapshot's own figures (TVL, seven-day growth, token-free age) and not a hardcoded list, concrete farm plans with costs and times, a sortable/filterable page with a detail view, and a page that looks made. The snapshot holds 758 protocols, 40 on the watchlist, floor $50M. My design: cover the watchlist plus EVERY pre-token launch candidate below the floor that passes the watchlist rule's own product tests (173 early finds, 213 rows), a category-rate value model (growth and maturity multipliers on top), seven-step category farm playbooks, live tokens separated into their own view, and a dark scope-themed dashboard whose data.js is written from the same board, so page and board cannot disagree. Writing the entrypoint first.

Screenshots render and sit inside every cap. Reviewing them against the judge's criteria, two improvements are worth making before this is final. First, the model is blind to distribution: CCIP records 21 chains and Steakhouse 11, yet reach counts for nothing, while a single-chain protocol with the same record scores the same - a launch's starting audience is a real part of its value, so I am adding a reach multiplier (+4% per chain beyond the first, capped at seven extra chains) to the model, its constants, the row breakdown and the header. Second, a smaller thing the detail screenshot shows: the value-math table's multiplier column wraps mid-number; the stylesheet needs nowrap there. The main.ts summary also deserves a top-5 line and an explicit screenshot byte-cap guard, so a bad render fails here and not at the gate.
